paragraphs: Fife Council's Family Based Care Service has its own fostering team, and several independent agencies listed below also approve carers who live in Fife. The council says every child has the right to grow up in a family, and it is looking for both full-time and part-time foster carers.

In 2025 the council made a particular appeal for carers for local children affected by disability, both to look after a child full time and to offer short breaks that give other foster carers, kinship carers and parents a rest. It says carers in this role get training and support from experienced carers and professionals.

According to the council, anyone over 21 with a spare bedroom can apply. You can be single or in a relationship, of any gender or sexual orientation, a parent or not, a renter or a homeowner, retired or working, and you can have pets. Council carers can join support groups including a men's group, a new carers group, a permanence group and a teenage support group, and more than 70 of them attended the annual Fife Foster Carers Conference in August 2026, which included workshops and wellbeing sessions.

The team holds a monthly online information session on the last Tuesday of each month and has run drop-in sessions in Dunfermline and Cupar libraries, where people can ask about the process, pay, training and common myths. The fostering team can be reached on 01383 602235. Compare what the council offers with two or three of the agencies below before you decide.
